The composed case: ~:parent~ / ~:parents~ become the parent-ids junction, each ~:args~ entry becomes a binding row on the inherited slot it targets — or, when the entry is ~{:type T …}~ with no binding markers, a NEW own slot on top of inheritance. Which of the two, and on which ancestor, is ~resolve-slot-owner~'s call.

Given a composed fn and an arg name, find the ancestor that DECLARED the slot — walking the inheritance chain, then the refs' trees, and disambiguating a name owned on both paths by type. This is the parse-time twin of the executor's ~build-lookups~: the same slot identity, computed once from EDN so the binding row carries the right ~slot-id~ before a single row is written.

* 12. load-impls-via-eval
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: packages/load-impls-via-eval
:FILE: src/graphden/packages/loader.clj
:LINE: 211
:MINS: 2.7
:END:

The counterpart to fns.edn: slurp ~impls.clj~, ~eval~ each form in a fresh namespace, and return that namespace's ~impls~ var — the ~{fn-name → impl-fn}~ map. How Clojure code on disk becomes live functions. The ~reuse-loaded-impls?~ arm is why coverage can see this layer at all: evaluating from the resource leaves cloverage with nothing to instrument, so under ~bb coverage~ the already- instrumented namespace is reused instead of re-evaluated.

* 16. sync-fn-entities-from-packages!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: packages/sync-fn-entities-from-packages!
:FILE: src/graphden/packages/sync.clj
:LINE: 1022
:MINS: 11.4
:END:

The other half of every boot, and the one the loader hands off to: sync composed fn-defs to storage, heal namespace-moved identities and reap retired ones nothing live references (~_anon-*~ shapes included; ~{:dry-run? true}~ previews the plan from a REPL), seed each fn-def's rich-type, then run the topological type-check sweep. Read the two long comments — the batch-size binding (a fresh-DB boot writes >10k fn rows past the guard meant for USER writes) and ~:skip-type-check?~ (~15s of sweep the test bootstrap may opt out of, production never does — which is precisely why ~bb type-sweep~ exists: EVERY fixture opts out, so before that check a corpus type regression surfaced only when a real instance booted). This is declarative sync: the packages on disk are the desired state, storage is reconciled toward it.

* 18. ref-kw
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: packages/ref-kw
:FILE: src/graphden/packages/export.clj
:LINE: 106
:MINS: 2.1

How a ref serializes: BARE keyword when the name is unique (canonical minimal form), namespace-QUALIFIED when it's duplicated across the export set. Qualification never falls back to bare — a version-materialized ~@~-ns qualifies as ~(keyword "lib@1-2-0.sub" n)~ and the root ns as ~(keyword "" n)~, both legal in-memory values even though no EDN reader could parse their printed form.

Publish lands the bundle IN the graph: an immutable, content-hashed ~:package-version~ row (name + semver + fns + declared deps). Install is its mirror — ~materialize-package-fns~ syncs the pinned version's fns into a version-qualified ~@~-namespace and writes a ~:package-install~ pin; update/rollback rewrites refs between versions; fork copies copy-on-write with no pin.

* 23. upsert-pin!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: packages/upsert-pin!
:FILE: resources/packages/registry/registry/impls.clj
:LINE: 349
:MINS: 2.6
:END:

Where the marketplace's install COUNT comes from (docs/MARKETPLACE.md). A new pin is an install and bumps the global ~:package-stat~ row with an atomic ~INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE~ over the pool — deliberately inside the pin write unit, like the invalidation an entity write owes, because a graph-side 'was it pinned?' probe is an effectful read a later ref would re-run AFTER the pin. Moving a pin (update / rollback) is not an install. Everything else the marketplace needs — listing normalisation, the cards' rating aggregate, the filters, the partials, the review upsert, the storefront bodies — is graph, four modules sharing the ~app.marketplace~ namespace: ~registry/marketplace{,-surface, -storefront,-moderation}/fns.edn~.

:LINE: 62

The operator's decision on a public listing (docs/MARKETPLACE.md § 8). Three things to notice: the platform-admin gate sits at the deepest effectful core so no route bypasses it; the read goes through ~registry-shared/platform-base~ — the storage BENEATH the org-scoped decorator, because the operator's own org would hide another org's pending row; and the updated row is raised through core's notification seam (~tc/notify! :package-moderated~), which the tenancy addon turns into the publisher's email. The module's impls file is small on purpose: identity, roster, semver, the origin card and moderation — everything else is graph.

The loaded-package ROSTER — recorded by ~load-packages~ itself, so boot and the test golden bootstrap leave the same read model. One row per package (version, description, base-fn count, ~impl+fns~ vs ~fns-only~, ~bundled~ vs ~manifest~); the marketplace's Executor tab lists it through ~:loaded-packages~. It is the honest answer to 'what does this executor run?' without offering to install a Type-2 package, which is code and enters through the build.

:LINE: 84
:MINS: 2.2

Why a fresh marketplace is not empty (docs/MARKETPLACE.md § 11). The starter catalogue — the platform's themes, keyboard layouts and example packages — is DATA (~starter-catalogue.edn~, in the publish route's own fields); this seed publishes each entry at boot through the very row a publish writes (~registry-shared/version-row~ + ~insert-or-exists!~, moved out of the publish impl so the two can never drift), in the platform tier, so it lands public + approved. Idempotent by (name, version), never over a name another org lists publicly. A change to a listing is a version bump: rows are immutable.

* 27. adopt-bundle-identities!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: packages/adopt-bundle-identities!
:FILE: src/graphden/packages/sync.clj
:LINE: 523
:MINS: 3.7
:END:

The WRITE half of the export/import pair — ~POST /api/import/graph~ applies an exported bundle to a NAMED branch. The route is a fn-def pipeline (~:import-bundle!~ in ~registry/registry/fns.edn~) over one-call primitives: find/create the target (owner-stamped, ~owner~ write-policy — the push-branch convention), skip package-owned defs, drop the anons only they reached, then THIS step — adopt editor-born same-name identities onto their deterministic ids — then the shared ~:sync-fn-defs-branch!~ (the MCP upsert's own), optionally a prune to snapshot semantics. Cross-install push/pull and git-snapshot restores all land here, then ride the normal diff → review → merge flow. Note the adoption repoints refs in the IDENTITY plane: it is why the MCP upsert does not run it.

* 28. reconcile-bundle-scope!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: packages/reconcile-bundle-scope!
:FILE: src/graphden/packages/sync.clj
:LINE: 566
:MINS: 4.7
:END:

Snapshot semantics for a runtime import (~?prune=true~): within exactly the bundle's namespaces, a deterministic-id fn the bundle no longer contains is TOMBSTONED on the branch (a ~:deleted-at~ version — so it hides an INHERITED fn too, not just a branch-local one, and the deletion propagates on merge). Never the boot reconciler's identity-plane purge, which would reach across branches. Referenced removals are kept + reported, loud.

The GIT face: a bundle laid out as one module file per namespace (the fns.edn module shape) + a manifest, byte-deterministic so a git diff is a graph diff. Read the seq-order printer note — the parser derives slot POSITIONS from map iteration order, so the printer must not 'canonicalise' nested keys. ~graphden.cli~ (export/import/push/pull) is the HTTP-only round-trip over this.

The graph's own linter, run over the same loader output at CI time (~bb graph-lint~): duplicate definitions — exact, and after inlining ~_~-private helpers — dead privates (unreferenced, and the cluster behind them), bindings that restate what a fn inherits, siblings that should share a parent, and over-deep chains. One engine over EDN-shape fn-defs, so the editor's per-branch graph is linted by the same code. docs/GRAPH_LINT.md.

The editor's side of the same engine: the per-ctx graph snapshot (org-sliced, branch-resolved) is rebuilt into loader-shaped fn-defs and linted, memoised per branch while that branch's snapshot object is unchanged. The ⚐ lint chip and the Inspector's Lint section share this one call; the suppressions it subtracts live in the graph as a ~:const~.
